chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Ali (peace be upon him) did not take the inheritance of any of his mawali upon their death if he had relatives; he would hand it over to his relatives.'
ai.seo_question: What was the practice of Imam Ali regarding the inheritance of mawali when they had living relatives?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) adherence to the principle of *qurbah* (kinship) over political or economic gain, demonstrating that the Imam prioritized the rights of natural relatives over his own status as the primary heir of the mawali. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly view that the Imam’s inheritance rights were not absolute but were subject to the same legal principles of equity and family ties that govern the community, reinforcing the legitimacy of his just governance.
